title: Dynamic proxies in frameworks
context: Where are dynamic proxies used in real frameworks?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java basics questions (3 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Frameworks use proxies to add behaviour around a call without changing the class. Spring uses them for `@Transactional`, `@Async`, security checks and caching. Its AOP advice runs before or after the proxied method. ORMs like Hibernate use lazy-loading proxies. Remote-call libraries generate a proxy from an interface, so a call on the interface becomes an HTTP or RPC request. The cost is that calls made from inside the same class skip the proxy.

points.title: Cross-cutting behaviour
points.why: Transactions, caching and security are added without editing business code.

points.title: Self-invocation bypasses proxies
points.why: A method calling another method on this skips the proxy, so its annotations don't apply.
